title: Conjecture 1.1
statement_text: For every $d\in\mathbb{Q}$, $d>1$, and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a graph $G$ with $$e(G)\leq Cn^{2-1/d}$$ edges which is $\mathcal{H}_{d}(n)$-universal, where $C=C(d)$.
context_text: A graph $G$ is universal for a family $\mathcal{H}$ if every $H\in\mathcal{H}$ is a (not necessarily induced) subgraph of $G$. The density of a graph $H$ is $m(H)=\max_{H'\subseteq H}e(H')/v(H')$, and $\mathcal{H}_d(n)$ is the family of all $n$-vertex graphs of density at most $d$ (it contains graphs of maximum degree at most $2d$, $d$-degenerate graphs and graphs of arboricity $d$; density at most $d$ implies $\lfloor2d\rfloor$-degeneracy). The authors initiate the study of universality for graphs of bounded density, aiming to unify results for bounded-degree graphs, forests and degenerate graphs. A counting argument shows $e(G)=o(n^{2-1/d})$ is not enough, even restricted to graphs of bounded maximum degree, so the conjectured bound would be optimal up to $C$. The condition $d>1$ is needed: for density at most $1$ (essentially forests) $\Theta(n\log n)$ edges are necessary and sufficient. Previously Allen, Böttcher and Liebenau gave $O_d(n^{2-1/\lfloor2d\rfloor}\log^{1/(2d)+o(1)}n)$. The authors construct $\mathcal{H}_d(n)$-universal graphs with $C(d)\,n^{2-1/(\lceil d\rceil+1)}$ edges; for the subfamily of graphs of maximum degree at most $D$ they obtain $n^{2-1/d}2^{C\sqrt{\log n}}$ edges for rational $d>1$, and the optimal $C(D,d)\,n^{2-1/d}$ when $d$ is an integer. They call this conjecture the main remaining open problem.
notes: The complete edge bound $e(G)\leq Cn^{2-1/d}$ appears in the introduction prose; the theorem-environment extraction was truncated. Statement reconstructed from the introduction.

title: Conjecture 1.6
statement_text: For every $D,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $d\in\mathbb{Q}$, $d\geq 1$, there exists a graph $G$ with $$e(G)\leq Cn^{2-1/d}$$ edges which is $\mathcal{H}_{d}^{D}(n)$-universal, where $C=C(D,d)$.
context_text: This is the bounded-maximum-degree analogue of Conjecture 1.1, where $\mathcal{H}_{d}^{D}(n)$ is the family of all $n$-vertex graphs with density at most $d$ and maximum degree at most $D$. The authors note that unlike the unbounded-degree case, no additional $\log n$ factor is expected to be necessary even for forests, so the condition is relaxed to $d\geq 1$. Proposition 1.2 shows the lower bound $e(G)\geq \alpha n^{2-1/d}$ holds in this setting, confirming the conjectured bound would be tight.
notes: The edge bound formula was truncated in the theorem-environment extraction; it is inferred from context (Proposition 1.2 lower bound and analogy with Conjecture 1.1) to be $e(G)\leq Cn^{2-1/d}$.
